name: Decode symbol relations
statement: \text{Decode each symbol into a relation, draw it on a family tree with gender marks, and read the relation between the two end persons.}
derivation: Write the code table once: e.g. $+$ = sister, $-$ = father, $\ast$ = wife, $\div$ = mother.
Read the chain two persons at a time: A + B means 'A is the sister of B'.
Draw parents above children, couples side by side (=), siblings on one row; mark each gender as soon as a relation fixes it.
A wife of the father is the mother; children of one person are siblings.
Trace the path from the reference person to the target and name it in their order.
visual_proof: The decoded chain drawn as a tree: each symbol becomes a vertical (parent-child), horizontal (sibling) or double (couple) line.

steps: C ÷ D: C is mother of D. D * E: D is wife of E, so D is female.
E - F: E is father of F, so D (his wife) is F's mother.
F ÷ G: F is mother of G, so F is female.
F is the daughter of C's daughter D: daughter's daughter (C).

common_traps: Reading 'A + B' backwards (B is sister of A) and getting the inverse relation.
Assuming a gender the code never fixed; G in 'F ÷ G' has no gender.
Stopping one step early: D is C's daughter, F is D's daughter, so F is C's daughter's daughter, not daughter.
Treating the father's wife as a step-relation instead of the mother.

diagram.alt_text: Family tree for A + B - C ÷ D * E - F ÷ G: A (female) sister of B (male); B father of C (female); C mother of D (female); D married to E (male); D and E parents of F (female); F mother of G.

name: Family tree diagram
statement: \text{Draw generations as rows, mark + (male) / - (female), join couples with =, then trace the path between the two persons.}
derivation: Put each statement on the tree as you read it; one generation per row.
Siblings share parents: if C is E's sister and A is C's parent, A is E's parent too.
A child's two parents are a couple, so their genders are opposite.
Name the relation from the reference person's side: 'G is A's ...' starts at A.
visual_proof: Generations stacked as rows: vertical lines for parent-child, = for couples, a horizontal bar for siblings.

steps: F is mother of E; C is sister of E, so C and E are F's children.
C is daughter of A, so A is E's parent too: A (+) is F's husband.
G is the brother of F.

common_traps: Naming the relation from the wrong end: 'wife's brother' versus 'sister's husband'.
Fixing gender from a name or from 'is the child of'; only words like brother, mother, wife fix it.
Missing that two children of one parent are siblings, so the second parent is shared.
Taking 'not the mother' as unknown instead of 'the father' when the person is a parent.

diagram.alt_text: Family tree: A (male) married to F (female); their children C (female) and E (male); G (male) is F's brother; E is father of K.

name: Pointing/introduction statements
statement: \text{Resolve the sentence from its end towards the speaker ('my father's only son' = the speaker if male), then name the pointed person's relation.}
derivation: Start at the speaker and the last 'my ...' phrase: 'my mother' is the speaker's mother.
Resolve each phrase in turn: 'only daughter of my mother' = the speaker's sister if the speaker is male, the speaker herself if female.
'My father's only son' = the speaker if the speaker is male; a brother if female.
Place the pointed person on that node ('his mother is ...') and read the relation to the speaker.
visual_proof: A three-generation tree built from the speaker outward: the speaker's mother on top, the speaker and the sister below, the boy under the sister.
common_traps: Taking 'my father's only son' as a brother when the speaker is male; it is the speaker.
Calling the sister's son a son or a cousin; he is a nephew.
Reading the relation from the pointed person's side instead of the speaker's.
Ignoring 'only': with an only daughter, a female speaker is that daughter herself.

diagram.alt_text: Ravi says 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother': Ravi's mother has two children, Ravi (male) and his sister; the boy is the sister's son, so Ravi's nephew.
